posts.title: Omarchy: Smudged Fingers, Not Clean Hands
posts.description: Nobody praised the first printed Bibles for their craftsmanship. The type wobbled. Ink bled through thin paper. Pages ran crooked off the press, and readers got ink on their fingers just holding the thing. Monks had spent centuries perfecting the opposite: manuscripts so precise they were closer to relics than books. Gutenberg's machine didn't beat that precision. It made precision beside the poin
